transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. 

I just... well, honestly, what made me finally make the appointment is that I feel like the warm part of me just sort of... shut off? I hope I'm explaining that right. Like, after my stocking shift at the store, I'll sit on the couch with my husband, or I'll try to watch my regular shows, and I know I should feel comfort, or even just a little happy to be home. But... I don't know, there’s just nothing there right now. 

I feel awful about it, honestly, like I'm doing something wrong. Does that... does that make sense to you? Is that something you see people for?
How long have you been feeling this way, like the warm part of you has shut off?

Um, I guess it's been... about three weeks now? Yeah, right around three weeks. 

There was this, um, accident at the store. A pallet collapsed in the back room and... it injured one of my coworkers. I feel a little silly even bringing it up, honestly, because I wasn't the one who got hurt. I was just right there when it happened. So I really shouldn't be making a big deal out of it, right? I know they had it much worse. 

But ever since that day, I've just felt this way. I hope I'm not overreacting by coming in to see you for something that didn't even happen to my own body. Is it okay that I'm still feeling weird about it after three weeks?
Are you still able to enjoy activities or hobbies that you normally found pleasurable before these past three weeks?

Um... no, not really. I guess... well, that's kind of what I was trying to explain earlier, about how it feels like the warm part of me just shut off. Like, sitting on the couch with my husband or watching my regular shows after work... those were always my favorite parts of the day. 

And I know I *should* feel happy doing them, or at least feel that normal comfort, you know? But when I try now, there's just... nothing there. I just feel kind of blank. I feel terrible about it, honestly, because I really am trying to enjoy things, I promise. I don't want to be a downer for my husband. 

Does... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm making sense.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

I'm so sorry, I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record right now. I really wish I could give you a better answer, I do. 

I've tried to think of other things to do, you know, hoping something will spark that comfort or happiness again, but... it really is just everything. That warm feeling is just turned off, no matter what I try to look forward to. Even if I try to do something nice for myself, there's just nothing there. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a more positive answer for you. I really am trying to snap out of it and find something to enjoy, I promise. Am I... am I helping you understand at all, or am I just repeating myself too much?
Do you often feel guilty about things that wouldn't normally bother you?

Um, guilty? I don't... I don't think so? I mean, I guess I feel a little bad about not being more upbeat around my husband right now, but that's just because I want to be a good partner, you know? 

I don't think I'm walking around feeling guilty about random things, though. At least, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Is... is that something I should be looking out for? I hope it's okay that I don't have a better example for you. I'm really trying to answer everything right.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Um, sad? No, I wouldn't say I feel sad. I mean, I know I just said I feel blank and I'm not enjoying things, but it's not like I'm sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I'm still getting up and going to work and doing what I need to do. 

I really try to keep a good attitude, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone. So, no, not sad. Just... just that blank feeling I mentioned. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not being confusing by saying I don't feel sad but I also don't feel happy. I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to care about?

Um, lost interest? I guess... I mean, I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do. I still go to work, I still take care of things around the house. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or neglecting my responsibilities, because I'm definitely not doing that. 

I know I said I feel kind of blank, but I still care about my husband and my job and making sure everything is taken care of. I'm really trying to keep up with it all. I just... I might not feel that spark right now, but I still care about doing a good job. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I really don't want to sound like I've just stopped caring about my life.
Are you able to experience pleasure when you're doing things that are typically considered enjoyable, like eating your favorite foods or spending time with loved ones?

Um, pleasure? I... I don't know if I'd use that word exactly. I mean, I try to enjoy things, I really do. But... I guess honestly, that's kind of what made me come in to see you. 

I just feel like the warm part of me sort of... shut off? Like, I'll sit with my husband in the evenings, or I'll try to watch my favorite shows after work, and I know I should feel comforted, or, you know, even just a little happy to be relaxing. But... there's just nothing there right now. It's just that blank feeling again. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible wife or anything. I really do love him, and I want to feel happy when we're together. I'm just... having a hard time feeling it right now. Is that... is that normal for what we're talking about? I'm trying so hard to just be normal again, I promise.
Are there any things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, like I said, I still try to do the things I usually do. I haven't completely stopped doing anything I used to like. I still cook dinner, I still try to watch my shows, I still go for walks when the weather is nice. 

I guess I'm just going through the motions a little bit more than usual, but I wouldn't say there's any specific thing I've just completely stopped enjoying or given up on. I'm really trying to keep my routine as normal as possible. I hope that's a good thing? I'm trying not to let this whole blank feeling take over my life, you know? Does that sound like I'm handling it okay?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Um, my weight? No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any changes. I mean, I try to make sure I'm still eating, even if I don't really feel like it sometimes. I know it's important to keep my strength up, especially for work. 

I haven't been stepping on the scale or anything, but my clothes still fit the same. So I think I'm doing okay there. I'm really trying to make sure I take care of myself so I don't cause any more problems. Is that... does that sound like I'm doing the right thing? I'm trying to be good about it.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I... I know things have been really off lately with that blank feeling, but I would never want to do anything like that. I promise. 

I know it would just cause so much pain for my husband, and I'd never want to do that to him. Plus, I need to keep my job at the warehouse going. I'm really just trying to get better and get back to being myself, not make things worse. 

I hope that's... I mean, that's a good sign, right? That I'm not having any thoughts like that? I'm really trying to do everything right here so I can just be normal again.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, with my job filling orders at the warehouse, you really have to keep up a pretty steady pace, and my supervisor hasn't said anything about me falling behind or anything like that. So I think I'm still moving just fine. And talking... no, I feel like I'm talking normally? 

I'm really trying hard not to let myself get sluggish or, you know, bogged down by everything. I just want to keep up and do my job right and not cause any delays. I hope I'm making sense? I just want to make sure I'm staying on track and doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

Um... maybe just a little? But I wouldn't say I'm falling apart or anything. I'm really trying to handle it well and not be a bother. I guess I've just been... extra careful? 

Like, especially when I'm anywhere near receiving now. I just find myself constantly checking the racks, and looking at the pallet height. I always need to know exactly where the exits are, and I keep checking to see who's moving behind me. It's like... I just feel like I can't trust the floor to be safe for even a minute right now. 

But I mean, safety is really important in a warehouse, right? So maybe it's actually a good thing that I'm being so thorough. I just want to make sure I'm being responsible and not letting my guard down. Does that... does that seem like a normal way to be? I'm just trying to do the right thing and be a good worker.
Do you often find yourself thinking you're to blame for things that aren't entirely your fault?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean... if I make a mistake at work, like pulling the wrong box or something, I definitely own up to it. I always want to be accountable for my own work, you know? But I don't think I blame myself for things that aren't my fault. 

I try to be really fair about that. Just... keeping a level head about what's actually on me and what isn't. I think I'm doing pretty good with that part, at least. That's the right way to look at it, isn't it? I'm really trying to just be reasonable and not overreact to things.
Do you feel depressed?

Um, depressed? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm still getting up every day and going to work, and I'm getting my job done. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? Even with everything being a bit stressful right now, I just want to keep a smile on my face and not bring anyone else down. 

I think I'm managing pretty well, honestly. I'm not sitting around crying or anything like that. I just want to be a productive person and keep moving forward. That's the best way to handle things, right? Just staying busy and not letting yourself get stuck in a rut. I really hope I'm doing this right.
Are you still able to feel a sense of enjoyment or pleasure when something good happens to you?

Um... well, I try to. I really do. I don't want to seem ungrateful or anything when good things happen. But... I guess, honestly, that’s actually kind of what made me come in to see you. 

I just feel like... um, like the warm part of me just sort of shut off? Like, I'll sit with my husband, or try to watch my favorite shows after work, and I know I should feel comforted, or even just a little happy... but there’s just nothing there right now. 

I feel terrible about it, because I want to be good company for him and I want to appreciate the good things. I'm not doing it on purpose, I swear. Does that... does that make me sound awful? I'm really trying to get back to normal and feel things the right way again, I promise.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Um, weight? No, I don't think so. I mean, I haven't really been checking the scale or anything, but my work uniform still fits the same. I'm pretty sure I look about the same as I always do. 

I always try to make sure I eat my meals, especially since my job keeps me on my feet a lot. I don't want to get weak and not be able to do my job right, you know? I think it's really important to keep your strength up. So, no, I haven't lost any weight. I hope that's a good sign, right? That means I'm taking care of myself okay?
Have you noticed any significant change in your appetite over the past three weeks?

Um, my appetite? No, I don't think it's changed much at all. I mean, I still make sure to eat breakfast before I go to the warehouse, and I pack my lunch every day just like I always do. 

I guess maybe I'm not craving my favorite snacks as much right now, but I still eat all my meals. I know it's really important to keep eating so I don't get sick or anything. I'm trying really hard to just keep my routine normal, you know? I want to make sure I'm doing all the right things to stay healthy. That's what I'm supposed to be doing, isn't it?
Do you feel like you're moving more quickly or slowly than you usually do?

Um, moving faster or slower? No, I don't think so. I mean, my job at the warehouse is pretty fast-paced, and I've been keeping up with all my quotas just fine. I make sure I get all my orders filled on time. 

I definitely haven't been slowing down or acting sluggish, I promise. I know my coworkers count on me, and I wouldn't want to drag the team down or make anyone think I'm slacking off. So I'm still moving around just like normal. That's a good thing, right? It means I'm still functioning okay?
